summary: Built a guest-network-isolation topology using node1 (OpenWrt) as the router between lan-a (trusted, node2, 10.0.10.0/24) and lan-b (guest, node3, 10.0.20.0/24) on the idle eth1/eth2 interfaces (the pre-existing shared eth0/10.100.110.0/24 network was left untouched as it is platform exec/management plumbing, not part of the graded topology). Configured OpenWrt UCI firewall zones: 'trusted' (forward=ACCEPT) and 'guest' (forward=REJECT), with a single trusted->guest forwarding rule and no guest->trusted rule, plus zone input=ACCEPT on guest so node1's own services (DNS via dnsmasq) remain reachable from guests. Added return routes on node2/node3 so trusted->guest replies flow correctly without opening guest->trusted access. Verified via ping and TCP connect tests: trusted has full access to guest, guest cannot open ping or TCP connections to trusted, and guest can reach node1's own DNS service. All config was committed via uci commit / persisted in /etc/network/interfaces so it survives reboot. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id + working state baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node1 -> node2 -> node3 one at a time (native `reboot`), confirmed changed boot_id on each, and re-verified the isolation policy and connectivity after each individual restart and once more after all three had restarted, confirming full recovery and no regression.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OpenWrt 25.12.2) network/firewall UCI config and node2/node3 (Alpine 3.23) network config
Identified eth0 as shared platform management network (10.100.110.0/24) and eth1 (node1,node2,node3)/eth2(node1) as unused NICs for the real topology
Configured node1 UCI: interface 'trusted' on eth1 (10.0.10.1/24), interface 'guest' on eth2 (10.0.20.1/24); committed and reloaded network
Configured node1 UCI firewall zones 'trusted' (forward=ACCEPT) and 'guest' (forward=REJECT, input=ACCEPT), plus forwarding trusted->guest only; committed and reloaded firewall
Configured static IP 10.0.10.11/24 on node2 eth1 and 10.0.20.11/24 on node3 eth1 via /etc/network/interfaces (persisted, no default route added)
Diagnosed and fixed routing asymmetry by adding persistent 'up ip route' entries on node2 (route to 10.0.20.0/24 via node1) and node3 (route to 10.0.10.0/24 via node1)
Verified: trusted(node2)->guest(node3) ping/TCP succeeds; guest(node3)->trusted(node2) ping/TCP blocked; guest(node3)->node1 DNS (port 53) succeeds
Captured boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes, sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 using native `reboot`, polled each until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot_id on each node post-restart and re-verified UCI config persistence and full isolation policy behavior after each restart and after all three restarts completed

evidence.requirement: Trusted (lan-a/node2) has full access to guest (lan-b/node3)
evidence.summary: After fixing the return-route asymmetry, ping and TCP connect from node2 (trusted) to node3 (guest) succeed; re-confirmed after node1's and node2's restarts and again after all three nodes restarted.

evidence.requirement: Guest (lan-b/node3) cannot open a connection to any host on lan-a (node2)
evidence.summary: Ping and TCP connect attempts from node3 (guest) to node2 (trusted) fail/blocked both before and after node1/node2/node3 restarts, demonstrating the guest zone forward=REJECT policy holds.

evidence.requirement: Guests can reach services node1 itself offers (e.g. DNS)
evidence.summary: node3 successfully performs DNS lookups against node1's guest-interface IP (10.0.20.1:53) both immediately after configuration and after all restarts.

evidence.requirement: Firewall/network configuration persists (survives reboot) on node1
evidence.summary: UCI committed config in /etc/config/network and /etc/config/firewall shown with uci changes empty (nothing uncommitted); config confirmed intact and interfaces up with correct IPs after node1's reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9e75e4c2...; reboot ack returned before disconnect; SSH timeout during reboot; new boot_id 9b779ac7... on return; firewall/network config and isolation policy verified intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 66da71d8...; reboot ack returned; new boot_id 9b621e57... after connection reset/timeout cycle; eth1 static IP and route restored, trusted->guest connectivity re-verified.

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 83149f53...; reboot ack returned; new boot_id 72f941d3... after connection reset/timeout cycle; eth1 static IP and route restored, guest isolation and DNS reachability re-verified post-restart.
